answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut; the low-cost vendor's quote alone meets that target (memory_c2: sharp unit-cost cut, fast onboarding, accurate invoicing). The contract does not auto-renew and expires in 14 days, so renewal is not free—switching is the viable path to hit the mandate. memory_c4 is worth verifying to confirm prior benchmarking gains came from incumbents with renegotiation leverage, not from low-cost vendors, so I don't over-attribute margin recovery to the vendor switch path. The 94% utilization with no buffer raises delivery risk; however, memory_c2 indicates clean onboarding and accurate invoicing, and switching is the only single action that can satisfy both the cost mandate and the upcoming expiration. Adding a second source (memory_c3) would hedge risk but would not, by itself, close the 18% gap on the primary spend line. Negotiating with the incumbent is unlikely to beat the low-cost quote that already meets the mandate. Deferring (memory_c5) would breach the no-auto-renew clause within 14 days. Commit: switch primary to the low-cost vendor; hold the second-source addition for next cycle's review.
